items.followUp: State two limitations of Bohr’s atomic model.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying a major limitation of Rutherford’s model.
rubric.description: Could not explain the stability of the atom.
rubric.how: State that orbiting electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus, so the model could not explain why atoms remain stable.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying the model’s failure to explain atomic spectra.
rubric.description: Could not explain the line spectra of atoms.
rubric.how: State that the model could not explain the discrete line spectrum emitted by atoms.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of the atom: orbiting electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus.
It also could not explain the line spectra emitted by atoms.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a group and a period in the periodic table.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for describing groups as vertical columns and/or their shared chemical features.
rubric.description: Groups are vertical columns in the periodic table; their elements have similar properties.
rubric.how: Identify a group as a vertical column, or state that elements in a group have similar properties.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for describing periods as horizontal rows and/or their shared number of electron shells.
rubric.description: Periods are horizontal rows; their elements have the same number of electron shells.
rubric.how: Identify a period as a horizontal row, or state that its elements have the same number of occupied shells.

modelAnswer: Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table; elements in a group have similar chemical properties.
Periods are the horizontal rows; elements in a period have the same number of electron shells.

items.followUp: What was the main aim of alchemists?

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for placing alchemy in its historical context as an early practice related to chemistry.
rubric.description: Alchemy was an early, historical practice related to chemistry.
rubric.how: Describe alchemy as an ancient or early practice.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for stating a characteristic aim of alchemists.
rubric.description: Alchemists sought to change base metals into gold (and also sought an elixir of life).
rubric.how: Mention the attempt to transform base metals into gold or the search for an elixir of life.

modelAnswer: Alchemy was an early practice related to chemistry.
Alchemists tried to convert base metals into gold and searched for an elixir of life.

items.followUp: Define electronegativity and state whether it has a unit.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for the defining idea of electronegativity.
rubric.description: Electronegativity is an atom’s ability to attract the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
rubric.how: State that an atom attracts shared or bonding electrons in a bond.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for correctly stating the unit status.
rubric.description: Electronegativity has no unit; it is dimensionless.
rubric.how: State that it has no unit or is dimensionless.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.
It has no unit; it is a dimensionless quantity.

items.followUp: Write two properties of polar covalent compounds.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for one standard physical property of non-polar covalent compounds.
rubric.description: They generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: State that their melting points or boiling points are generally low.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for another standard property, such as electrical conductivity or solubility.
rubric.description: They generally do not conduct electricity; many are insoluble in water and soluble in non-polar solvents.
rubric.how: Give one valid property distinct from low melting/boiling points.

modelAnswer: Non-polar covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They do not conduct electricity; many are insoluble in water and dissolve in non-polar solvents.

items.followUp: Why is the covalent bond in Cl₂ non-polar?

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying why the bonded atoms attract electrons equally.
rubric.description: The two hydrogen atoms are identical and have the same electronegativity.
rubric.how: State that the atoms are identical or have equal electronegativity.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for explaining the resulting electron distribution or lack of polarity.
rubric.description: The shared electron pair is distributed equally, so no poles develop.
rubric.how: State that equal sharing means the bond has no positive and negative poles.

modelAnswer: The two hydrogen atoms are identical and have the same electronegativity.
They share the bonding pair equally, so no positive or negative poles develop in the H₂ molecule.

items.followUp: Define crystalline solids and give two examples.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for describing the regular, ordered arrangement characteristic of crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Crystalline solids have particles arranged in a regular, orderly pattern.
rubric.how: State that their particles have a regular arrangement or that they have a definite geometrical shape.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for giving two correct examples of crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Examples include sodium chloride and diamond.
rubric.how: Give two valid examples; the model answer gives sodium chloride and diamond.

modelAnswer: Crystalline solids are solids whose particles are arranged in a regular, orderly pattern, giving them a definite geometrical shape.
Examples include sodium chloride (NaCl) and diamond.

items.followUp: Explain how increasing external pressure affects the boiling point of a liquid.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for stating the effect of external pressure on boiling point.
rubric.description: Increasing external pressure raises the boiling point; decreasing pressure lowers it.
rubric.how: State the correct direction of change between external pressure and boiling point.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for explaining boiling in terms of vapour pressure and external pressure.
rubric.description: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure.
rubric.how: State that boiling occurs when vapour pressure reaches or equals the external pressure.

modelAnswer: Increasing the external pressure raises the boiling point of a liquid; decreasing the pressure lowers it.
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
